chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Baseer and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Charity is the dirt of the hands of the people, and Allah has prohibited for me from it, and from other than it, that which He has prohibited, and indeed, charity is not permissible for the children of Abdul Muttalib.'

Then he said: 'By Allah, if I were to stand at the door of Paradise and grab its ring, you would know that I would not prefer anyone over you. So be pleased with yourselves for what Allah and His Messenger are pleased with for you.' They said: 'We are pleased.'
ai.seo_question: Why is charity prohibited for the Prophet and the Banu Abdul Muttalib?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the prohibition of *sadaqah* (general alms) for the Banu Hashim, distinguishing it from *zakat* and highlighting the Prophet's unique status as free from the 'impurity' of worldly accumulation. The Imam's subsequent pledge to prioritize the community's welfare even at the gates of Paradise underscores the theological concept of *Fadl* (superiority) and the expectation of contentment (*Rida*) with divine decree, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding the distribution of wealth to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim and Abu Baseer and Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The charity is the dirt of the hands of the people, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Prohibited upon me<sup>saww</sup> from it, and from other that which what has been Prohibited; and the charity is not Permissible for the Clan of Abdul Muttalib’.

Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! If I<sup>saww</sup> were to stand at the Door of the Paradise, then grab its ring, you would come to know that I<sup>saww</sup> would not prefer (anyone else) over you. Therefore, be pleased with what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> are pleased with’. They said, ‘We are pleased’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, abu Basir and Zurarah who have said the following: “Abu Ja’far and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, have said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Charity is filth of the hands of people. Allah has prohibited me to accept it and certain other things for my own use. Charity is not lawful for the children of ‘Abd al-Muttalib.’

He then said, ‘By Allah, when I will stand at the door of Paradise and get hold of its handle, you must know that I will not give preference to others before you. Thus, you should be happy with what Allah and His Messenger have decided for you.’ They (children of ‘Abd al-Muttalib) then said, ‘We are happy with your decision.’”
